summary: The paper's institutional claims are mostly checkable only against facts it supplies itself. I found one material event-timing inconsistency. The Figure 1 caption, and the abstract's "two actual openings" claim, treat Grettefoss Bridge as a planned opening that did not occur. Table 2 footnote c states that it was confirmed to have opened on 3 November 2026. Other institutional details are internally consistent and consistent with public knowledge: Norway's 15 counties, Agder as county number 42, Grimstad's municipality number 4202, Flesberg, the NVDB road-owner category "F", and 5 October 2026 falling on a Monday. The Gemini 3.8 Flash model exists, with a Google model card. I could not verify the NVDB field semantics, the FINN.no coverage claim, the Retriever/Atekst coverage claim or the specific project facts from authoritative sources. The NVDB API documentation only shows startdato as a version-validity date and lists no opening-date field. That supports the paper's description but does not establish it, so I report no finding on it.

findings.finding_summary: Figure 1 and the abstract count only two openings that took place, but Table 2 footnote c says Grettefoss Bridge was confirmed to have opened on 3 November 2026. The paper's own event-status information therefore gives three realised openings.

findings.claim_text: Only 2 of 70 search hits concern a cycling infrastructure opening that actually took place; the two further openings (Tromsø Bridge and Grettefoss Bridge) are only planned.
findings.evidence_summary: Figure 1 (p. 4) says only 2 openings 'actually took place' and describes Tromsø and Grettefoss as 'planned'. The abstract says the pilot 'contained only two actual openings'. Table 2 on p. 5 (inspected in the retained page image) lists Grettefoss Bridge with status 'Planned' and opening date 3 Nov 2026, but footnote c reads 'Confirmed to have opened 3 November as planned.' By the paper's own account the opening therefore occurred. The 'planned' label and the count of two are correct only as of the articles' publication dates (pilot window 2 Sep-10 Oct 2026). The caption states neither this qualification nor the later status. This matters for the headline noise ratio (2 of 70 hits), because status was updated for only some projects: footnote b records Tromsø's delay as of 6 November. It also bears on the planned-versus-actual date rule in Section 3.1.4. I did not check local-news or road-authority records for the real events, so this finding relies on the manuscript's internal statements.

findings.suggested_fix: State in the abstract, the Figure 1 caption and Section 3.1.2 that the counts are as of article publication or the extraction date. Report separately the later-confirmed status of Grettefoss (opened 3 November 2026) and Tromsø (delayed to 27 November), or update the status for all pilot projects at one stated reference date. Reconcile the status label 'Planned' in Table 2 with footnote c. If the aim is to show what share of hits concern openings that took place, say whether Grettefoss should count.

notes: The manuscript is dated November 2026 and describes events from September to November 2026. Specific project facts, such as the Homborsund, Stod, Tromsø Bridge and Grettefoss Bridge openings, and the NVDB record values, could not be checked against external records.

The NVDB API v4 documentation shows startdato and sluttdato only as version-validity dates in JSON examples. It lists no opening-date field. The documentation fetched did not define the fields, so the paper's statement that NVDB records only geometry registration is neither confirmed nor refuted.
